editorialReading: TTF has extended its retreat this week, falling to approximately €54.58/MWh on 4 August — breaking below the €57 floor of recent weeks — before partially recovering toward €57–59 on 5 August. The gas dip offers only modest comfort: above €55/MWh European ammonia production economics remain structurally challenged, and the monthly Tampa ammonia contract — the global benchmark for traded ammonia — has just confirmed August at approximately $870/t, up $70/t from July's $800/t. For the European nitrogen complex, that combination is paradoxical: the feedstock cost signal from TTF is marginally more benign than last week, yet the import-parity reference for ammonia — the floor under European plant economics — has hit a new Hormuz-cycle high. BASF, Yara, and OCI continue to face the same structural calculus: even at €54–58/MWh TTF, European ammonia production economics remain marginal, and the August Tampa fix reinforces that structural dependency on non-EU supply is deepening into the autumn application window. EU gas storage at approximately 54% full versus 65% last year leaves the continent acutely exposed to any further Middle East escalation. Urea is consolidating near $450–475/t and DAP is holding around $755–760/st, with China's phosphate export restrictions continuing to provide a floor through August. With ammonia at a Hormuz-cycle high and gas markets volatile in the €54–60 range, EU nitrogen economics continue to be squeezed from both the feedstock and import-competition sides simultaneously.
watchNext: Whether the August Tampa ammonia settlement at ~$870/t signals broader nitrogen cost re-pricing into the EU autumn application window — and whether September's contract holds or extends the Hormuz-cycle high. Whether TTF consolidates in the €54–60/MWh range or resumes its rise above €57 — the key threshold for EU ammonia plant economics. Whether urea sustains near the top of the $450–475 range or resumes its recovery. India / China urea tender activity and export policy changes remain the physical swing factor. Sourcing note: real-time Argus / ICIS / Green Markets assessments are subscription-only and the free World Bank Pink Sheet lags ~a month — these are publicly-cited indications.
